title: AUC Pair Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AUC
ROC Curve
Discrimination
Predictive Fidelity
description: A p5.js explorer that shows 40 synthetic learners sorted by forecast beside their ROC curve, moves a cutoff along both, and draws random successful-unsuccessful pairs whose running win fraction converges on the AUC.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: AUC as a pairwise ranking probability
learningObjectives: Explain AUC as the probability that a random successful learner outranks a random unsuccessful one, by connecting the ROC curve to a live count of correct pairs.

accessibility.colorBlindSafePalette: Okabe-Ito bluish green circles (correct) and orange squares (incorrect)

simulation.modelType: Seeded synthetic cohort with pairwise AUC and ROC computed in the sketch
equations: score = z + delta/2 (correct) or z - delta/2 (incorrect), z from seeded +z/-z normal pairs
AUC = (wins + 0.5 ties) / (24 x 16) over all green-orange pairs
assumptions: All data are synthetic: 24 correct and 16 incorrect held-out answers.
Seed 6 gives AUC 0.742 at signal 0.6; the symmetric draws give exactly 0.5 at signal 0.
Forecasts are rank scores and are not calibrated.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Two representations of one quantity, linked by live counts
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Step-through pair draws with a convergence plot and a linked cutoff
keyQuestions: How often does a random successful learner get the higher forecast?
Why does the running fraction of pairs won approach the area under the ROC curve?
Why does moving the cutoff not change the AUC?
commonMisconceptions: AUC is the accuracy at the best cutoff.
An AUC of 0.5 means half the forecasts are right.
A model with a high AUC must be well calibrated.
assessmentOpportunities: Explain an AUC value in plain words to a teacher.
Explain why signal 0 gives an AUC of 0.5.
